sources.title: Where to begin with giallo
sources.basis: Chris Gallant traces the Italian murder-mystery tradition and identifies these films within it. Genre boundaries are treated as flexible.

sources.title: The Strange Gialli of Sergio Martino
sources.basis: Alexandra Heller-Nicholas discusses the films as Martino gialli, supporting selections beyond Argento and Bava.

sources.title: The Forbidden Gialli of a Filmmaker Above Suspicion
sources.basis: Alexandra Heller-Nicholas identifies both films within Luciano Ercoli's giallo trilogy.

sources.title: Where to begin with folk horror
sources.basis: Adam Scovell outlines the British formative trio, landscape and isolation, then discusses these later examples.

sources.title: All the Haunts Be Ours: A Compendium of Folk Horror, Volume One
sources.basis: All three appear in the distributor's folk-horror collection curated by Kier-La Janisse. This is curatorial evidence, not a current streaming claim.

sources.title: Midsommar
sources.basis: Official synopsis establishes the remote Swedish festival and secluded community; the folk-horror placement is editorial interpretation of these elements.

sources.title: The Wailing
sources.basis: Official synopsis establishes a rural village, supernatural illness and a shaman. Placement follows those folk-horror elements.

sources.title: The Ritual
sources.basis: Official synopsis establishes the Swedish wilderness and a malevolent presence. The collection classification is editorial, not an exact Netflix genre label.

sources.title: Gareth Evans biography in Havoc announcement
sources.basis: The director biography explicitly identifies Apostle as a British folk-horror film.

sources.title: 10 great Irish horror films
sources.basis: Anton Bitel discusses the village's resurrection ritual within folk horror.

sources.title: 10 great body horror films
sources.basis: Matthew Thrift selects these films for bodily mutation and transformation. The Fly entry discusses its practical effects.

sources.title: Where to begin with David Cronenberg
sources.basis: Stephen Puddicombe connects the films to Cronenberg's recurring concern with bodily vulnerability, mutation and technology.

sources.title: The Thing (1982)
sources.basis: BFI describes assimilation and imitation, and identifies Rob Bottin's special makeup effects.

sources.title: A great horror film for every year
sources.basis: The 1988 entry discusses the consuming creature and Tony Gardner's special-effects work, supporting the body-horror selection.

sources.title: From Beyond
sources.basis: The official release describes Stuart Gordon's Lovecraft adaptation and documents its effects crew and bodily creature effects.

sources.title: 10 Defining Moments in Body Horror
sources.basis: The Society discussion identifies Screaming Mad George's special effects and the film's climactic bodily transformations.

sources.publisher: Mondo / Focus Features / Back Lot Music
sources.title: Raw Original Soundtrack
sources.basis: The licensed soundtrack release describes Julia Ducournau's film as coming-of-age body horror.

sources.title: 10 great horror films of the decade so far
sources.basis: The Substance entry explicitly discusses Coralie Fargeat's body horror.

sources.title: 10 great technothrillers
sources.basis: The entry describes organic game technology and spinal connections; this supports its inclusion at the intersection of body horror and science fiction.

sources.title: 10 great found-footage films
sources.basis: Billie Walker includes these examples, covering mock broadcasts, documentary forms and recovered recordings.

sources.title: The Outwaters: this found-footage horror takes no prisoners
sources.basis: Kim Newman uses Paranormal Activity (2007) as a comparison when discussing the narrative construction of found-footage horror.

sources.title: The Borderlands (AKA Final Prayer)
sources.basis: Official distributor confirms the alternate title, director and Vatican-investigation premise. Found-footage placement is editorial.

sources.title: The Medium
sources.basis: The official catalog synopsis describes the documentary team following a Thai shaman and filming her niece's changing behavior.

sources.title: Rob Savage on video call horror Host
sources.basis: A direct interview with the director documents the Zoom production; the introduction identifies the film as found footage.

sources.title: Gonjiam: Haunted Asylum
sources.basis: The official distributor synopsis describes a horror web-show crew livestreaming from the asylum.

sources.title: The Bay
sources.basis: The official distributor identifies the reconstructed outbreak through phone videos, emergency calls and webcams.

sources.title: Hell House LLC
sources.basis: Official synopsis identifies the found-footage investigation of deaths at a haunted attraction. No availability is inferred from this legacy detail page.

sources.title: 9 Alien Abduction Films with Deeper Meanings
sources.basis: The essay discusses these abduction narratives. They are film stories; claims of real abduction are not presented as verified facts.

sources.title: Christopher Walken: In The Lead
sources.basis: The Communion section describes Walken's portrayal of a writer grappling with a perceived extraterrestrial encounter.

sources.title: The Fourth Kind
sources.basis: Official synopsis identifies the fictional film's alien-abduction premise. Its publicity's real-case framing is not endorsed or repeated in the card copy.

sources.title: No One Will Save You
sources.basis: Official synopsis describes Brynn's confrontation with extraterrestrial beings.

sources.title: Nope: the horrors of being seen
sources.basis: Ben Walters places the film in the UFO-picture tradition. The card avoids revealing the nature of its aerial threat.

sources.title: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
sources.basis: Official synopsis distinguishes sightings, evidence and direct contact. Included as a contact film with suspense, not as an abduction-horror label.

sources.title: In Pod We Trust: Revisiting Invasion of the Body Snatchers
sources.basis: The essay identifies the 1978 film's extraterrestrial replacement and takeover premise.

sources.title: Invaders from Mars Blu-ray
sources.basis: Official BFI release identifies the 1953 film, a child's sighting and the adults changed by invading creatures.

sources.title: The 50 best films of 2020
sources.basis: The entry identifies the radio-signal mystery as a retro UFO tale. The metadata year 2019 reflects the festival premiere, not the 2020 general release.

sources.title: 10 great films about aliens visiting Earth
sources.basis: Paul O'Callaghan discusses invasion in Attack the Block and an extraterrestrial predator's perspective in Under the Skin.

sources.title: Altered (2006)
sources.basis: Official distributor confirms the 2006 year, director and former abductees capturing the alien responsible for their ordeal.

sources.title: Signs (2002)
sources.basis: BFI confirms the film, director and year. Its invasion-story placement is editorial and supported by the separate saved film metadata synopsis.
